sources.headline: Israeli police detain 10 people in rare raid against West Bank settlers
sources.text: Israeli police have detained 10 people in a rare raid against settlers, after a weekend of extreme violence in the occupied West Bank including an attack on US photojournalist Heidi Levine, which she described as an “attempted lynching”.She was knocked down, kicked and beaten by a group of masked Israeli men as she covered the olive harvest in a Palestinian village on Friday. The militants broke four vertebrae and a rip, ripped open her finger so it required surgery and left her with lacerations across her body.“I was practically, basically lynched by a gang of Jewish settlers in the area of Ramallah,” Levine said, in an interview with the BBC from her hospital bed on Monday.The day after that assault, Israeli militants armed with sticks and iron bars attacked a group of European diplomats and Palestinians harvesting olives outside the town of Taybeh, assaulting a visiting French mayor, smashing the window of an official car, and causing severe injuries to a young Palestinian man.The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, questioned the accounts of Israeli militant violence, ignoring extensive video and witness evidence.He referenced an “alleged attack” on Levine, whose severe injuries were visible in interviews from her hospital bed, and “unproven allegations” the diplomats had been targeted by militants.The attacks and his response drew a furious international reaction, including from the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee – generally considered a staunch ally of the current Israeli government – European nations and the editor of the Washington Post, Matt Murray.On Monday morning Israeli police released footage of a rare raid on settlers, and said they had detained 10 people connected with the attacks on foreigners and construction of an illegal outpost.Hours later a court extended the detention of six men connected with the attacks on foreigners, to between three and four days.There has been little response to extreme violence against Palestinians across the West Bank, and Levine said the global focus on her attack highlighted extreme double standards.“People are dealing with this, undergoing attacks, losing property, losing family members, being injured all across the West Bank and nothing is being done,” she said.Israelis target Palestinians with near total impunity in the occupied West Bank, where arrests are unusual, indictments rare and convictions even more unusual.Israeli human rights group Yesh Din has documented 561 incidents of settler and soldier violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank over three weeks since 27 September. That is an average of more than 26 each day.“It is telling that it took attacks on foreign nationals to prompt a significant response from Israeli authorities,” said the group’s executive director, Ziv Stahl. “Palestinians have endured years of systematic settler violence, with 94% of investigations into cases of settler violence against Palestinians closed without indictments.Levine said her body armour and helmet had prevented even more serious injuries, and she considered herself “lucky” given the ferocity of the attack. Netanyahu’s attempt to cast doubt on the attack felt like a “a big slap on my face”, she added.Netanyahu’s statements, apparently undermined by security forces arrests days later, were widely seen as an attempt to court far-right voters inside Israel, as the country heads into the final days of an election campaign.His coalition partners include extremist settlers, who support the campaign of violence that has driven thousands of Palestinians from their homes and land in the occupied West Bank over the last three years.Haaretz reported on Monday that political pressure was preventing the army from confronting “Jewish terrorism” in the West Bank, even when the targets were foreigners including diplomats and journalists.Commanders are reluctant to challenge settler leaders, or take action against Israeli civilians and soldiers who attack Palestinians, Israeli defence officials told the paper.Formal investigations and disciplinary procedures are limited and undermined by unofficial but clear messages of support from top commanders, the report said.It cited the response to an attack on a CNN crew in March. Central Command chief Maj Gen Avi Bluth suspended the battalion responsible from operational duty and announced disciplinary action against soldiers involved.Later that night, the brigade commander came to a base where the soldiers were staying to express his support and join them in prayer, Haaretz said.

sources.text: Israel has faced pressure, including from the United States, to investigate the attacks. Rights groups say most inquiries into extremist assaults on Palestinians go nowhere.

sources.headline: Arrests over Israeli settler attacks on US photojournalist and European diplomats in West Bank
sources.text: Ten suspects have been arrested in connection with recent violence in the West Bank including attacks on an ​American ⁠photojournalist and European ⁠diplomats, Israeli police have said.

sources.headline: U.S. lauds Israel for arresting 10 over West Bank settler attacks
sources.text:
By
Dov Lieber
Senior Reporter
Dov Lieber is a senior reporter for CBS News based in Tel Aviv, covering political, diplomatic and security developments across Israel, the Palestinian Territories and the broader Middle East.
Read Full Bio
October 19, 2026 / 9:56 AM EDT
/ CBS News
Add CBS News on Google
Tel Aviv — Israeli police announced on Monday the arrest of 10 people suspected to have taken part in recent violent attacks on Palestinians, an American photojournalist and European diplomats in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.The arrests come amid an avalanche of criticism, including from some senior U.S. officials, directed at Israel over repeated violent attacks by groups of mostly young Israeli settlers targeting Palestinians and others in the West Bank. The announcement of the arrests came as more violence against Palestinians in the occupied territory was reported Monday.Israeli police said officers working in conjunction with the Shin Bet domestic security and intelligence agency conducted a pre-dawn raid in the West Bank to locate individuals suspected of involvement in the violence and of violating a military commander's order declaring a closed military zone.
Israeli soldiers survey the scene as Israeli settlers gather while Palestinian farmers harvest their olives in the Israeli-occupied West Bank village of Deir Abu Mashal, Oct. 19, 2026.
ilia YEFIMOVICH/AFP/Getty
The arrests, dubbed Operation Olive Leaf by the police, came in the wake of multiple reported attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians as they worked on the annual olive harvest."Items linking the suspects to the alleged offenses were seized, and several vehicles were confiscated," the police said in a statement after the arrests.On Friday, several Palestinians and Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine were injured when a group of masked Israeli men attacked Palestinians harvesting olives in the West Bank, according to videos, eyewitnesses and Palestinian authorities.
On Saturday, European officials and the Israeli military said a diplomatic convoy with representatives from France, Belgium and Poland was assaulted by masked individuals near the Palestinian village of Taybeh.U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, in a social media post on Monday, called the arrests "a very positive development in finding & punishing those who severely attacked and beat Heidi Levine an unarmed journalist."Over the weekend, Huckabee called the attack on Levine an "act of terror carried out by masked cowards."
Heidi Levine, a photojournalist with the Washington Post, speaks to journalists at the hospital after sustaining multiple injuries during an attack by Israeli militant settlers on Palestinians harvesting olives, in Ramallah in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, Oct. 16, 2026.
Ali Sawafta/REUTERS
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio also condemned the attack on Levine Saturday, saying President Trump didn't want to see a crisis in the West Bank.
"We've asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff," Rubio said.Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office, in a statement on Saturday, urged people to exercise caution before drawing conclusions about the reported attacks on the European diplomats.Netanyahu's office noted that video published online of the incident appeared to show masked individuals confronting a diplomatic vehicle and others showed a smashed car window and someone lying on the ground, but it said those images alone did "not establish the complete sequence of events or individual responsibility."Israel's military said the diplomatic convoy was not coordinated with the defense forces, and that such coordination would've provided more safety, but it did not deny that the convoy came under attack by settlers.On Monday, new attacks on Palestinians by Israel settlers were reported by WAFA, the official media arm of the Palestinian Authority, which governs most Palestinians in the West Bank but has limited control over security in the occupied territory.Two Palestinians were injured in the villages of Turmus Ayya and Deir Abu Mash'al, northwest of Ramallah, amid attempts by individuals to set homes on fire by torching vehicles in front of the buildings, WAFA reported.
A Palestinian resident looks at the shattered glass of his home following a reported attack by Israeli settlers in the Israeli-occupied West Bank village of Turmus Ayya, Oct. 19, 2026.
ilia YEFIMOVICH/AFP/Getty
On Sunday night, Israel's military said several Israeli civilians entered the Palestinian village of Wadi a-Rahim in the West Bank, sprayed graffiti and set fire to a storage shed. The military said it had begun dismantling an illegal Israeli settler outpost in the area.
Violence by Israeli settlers targeting Palestinians in the West Bank has surged in recent years. Statistics released by the United Nations humanitarian office show that it started ramping up after Netanyahu took office in 2022 at the head of Israel's most far-right-wing coalition government in modern history in late 2022. The attacks have intensified in the wake of the war in Gaza, and amid strong support from some members of Netanyahu's cabinet for settlement expansion, and even for the West Bank to be completely annexed by Israel.

sources.headline: European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers in West Bank
sources.text: Image source, ReutersImage caption, Masked settlers are accused of attacking the convoyByDiplomatic correspondentReporting fromJerusalemUpdated 18 October 2026A delegation of European diplomats has been attacked by masked Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.Belgium condemned the assault on its consul general and the other envoys, while France decried the attack as "appalling". Both called for Israel to bring those responsible to justice.The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) also condemned what they called "the severe act of violence" and said they were investigating.But the office of the Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cast doubt on what happened, suggesting it was part of a "co-ordinated campaign to smear Israel".The attack came only a day after a number of Palestinians and Heidi Levine, a Washington Post photographer, were injured in a separate assault by settlers in another village in the West Bank.US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the attack on Levine was "disturbing" and "not a good look".It was also condemned by the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, who called it a "despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards". A staunch ally of Israel, Huckabee said the assailants must face "prosecution to the fullest extent of the law".Figure caption, Rubio 'very disturbed' over video of West Bank settler attack on US journalistIn Saturday's incident, the European diplomats - from Belgium, France, Poland and the Catholic Church - had come to the largely Christian village of Taybeh near Ramallah.They were there to assess the situation on the ground after almost near daily attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians trying to bring in their olive harvest.Video footage from the scene showed masked settlers confronting the convoy. Reports suggest stones were thrown.The Belgian authorities said a car from its consulate had a window smashed and a French mayor was assaulted. Video showed a man wearing a French tricolor sash slumped beside a vehicle.Belgium's foreign minister Maxime Prevot condemned the attack and said Israel had a responsibility to bring those responsible to justice, as well as ensuring the safety of diplomats, journalists and Palestinians."Palestinians face this violence every day. Settlers also target journalists reporting on it and diplomats. Harvesting olives, reporting the news or carrying out diplomatic duties should never put anyone at risk of attack," he said. He also said Belgium will continue to press for EU sanctions against those responsible for the violence.Image source, EPAImage caption, Palestinians have been harvesting olives in the West Bank this week before Israeli settlers attackFrance's Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot echoed those sentiments, calling on Israeli authorities to "urgently halt this criminal violence and guarantee the safety of civilian populations".Poland's foreign affairs ministry also called for a "firm response" from Israeli authorities and for "an end to the spiral of violence in the West Bank".The EU condemned the attacks, urged Israel to abide by international and human rights law, and end the expansion of settlements.A spokesperson said that while they acknowledged some Israeli officials had condemned the attacks, they said they still expect "full accountability as well as effective measures" to stop the continued violence against Palestinians and journalists.Gideon Sa'ar, Israel's foreign minister, said he strongly condemned the violence by what he called "Israeli rioters". He said the foreign ministry was in contact with the ambassadors of the countries involved.But he added: "Without detracting from the severity of the incident, it is unfortunate that the visit was not coordinated with the IDF in advance. Such coordination could have helped safeguard the visitors' security."The IDF said they "strongly condemn the severe act of violence that took place in the area of Taybeh, during which diplomatic representatives were attacked by Israeli rioters.""According to a preliminary inquiry, no IDF soldiers were present at the scene at the time of the attack," they added.Image source, ReutersImage caption, Netanyahu's office named the injured French official as Bernard Baudoux, the left-wing mayor of Aulnoye-AymeriesBut Netanyahu's office urged "caution before drawing conclusions" from reports about the attack.It said the images on social media "do not establish the complete sequence of events or individual responsibility".A statement continued: "Those circumstances remain under investigation. Israeli police and forensic investigators have launched an investigation to establish the facts and identify those responsible."It added that "these reports come amid concerns about a coordinated campaign to smear Israel and the Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria during the annual olive harvest, relying on sensational headlines before the full facts emerge".Netanyahu's office named the injured French official as Bernard Baudoux. The left-wing mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France told the AFP news agency the attack showed a tolerance by Israel's right-wing government for settler violence.The mayor said the settlers kicked him and beat him with iron bars, throwing him to the ground."It's the gratuitous nature of the violence that stuns me," he said. "They arrived completely enraged.""The whole world needs to know what's happening there. For me, I'll go back to my country and everything will be fine. Those who continue to suffer the most are those who are here," he said.

sources.headline: US visit after settler attacks: Officials go to Taybeh; violence keeps rising
sources.text: US Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labor Riley Barnes and US Ambassador to the Holy See Brian Burch, visit the Christian Palestinian village of Taybeh near Ramallah, a day after Israeli militant settlers attacked a French mayor and European diplomats during olive harvest, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.US diplomats visited the Christian Palestinian town of Taybeh in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Sunday after masked Israeli settlers attacked European diplomats and a French mayor near the village a day earlier. The visit came amid a surge in settler violence across the territory, with a US photojournalist also hospitalised after being assaulted while covering an olive harvest.Riley Barnes, assistant secretary of state for democracy, human rights and labour, and Brian Burch, US ambassador to the Holy See, visited the Latin Convent church in Taybeh. They were also expected to meet members of the local Christian community.The visit followed Saturday's attack on Belgian, French and Polish diplomats, a French mayor and Palestinian civilians near Taybeh. On Friday, Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was taken to hospital after being assaulted while covering a Palestinian olive harvest near another West Bank village.Despite the incidents, Israeli authorities had not announced any arrests by Sunday.Netanyahu cautious on settler violenceIsraeli foreign minister Gideon Saar and the Israeli military (IDF) blamed "Israeli rioters" for Saturday's attack on the diplomats. However, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the diplomats had entered a "sensitive area with a history of confrontations without prior coordination with the IDF".He also said the facts of the attack on Levine were "unclear".France urged Israeli authorities to arrest those responsible for Saturday's attack and end criminal violence in the West Bank.The US diplomats' visit also coincided with US President Donald Trump endorsing Netanyahu, his ally, for Israel's parliamentary election on October 27.Trump has opposed settlement expansion this year. However, his administration has put little pressure on Netanyahu's right-wing, pro-settler government to change its policy.Settler attacks surge across West BankViolence by Israeli settlers against Palestinians has been rising, with at least 170 attacks recorded since September 27, according to Israeli human rights group Yesh Din. Journalists, activists and foreign observers have also been targeted. Prosecutions of Israeli settlers remain rare.On Sunday, Reuters saw at least 10 masked settlers dressed in black throwing rocks at Palestinians and activists harvesting olives near the Palestinian town of Salfit in the West Bank. The farmers fled the area. Israeli border police were present and fired tear gas towards the hills.The West Bank is home to around 500,000 Israeli settlers and at least three million Palestinians.The United Nations and most countries consider Israeli settlements in the territory illegal under international law. Israel rejects this position, arguing that the territory is disputed rather than occupied.

sources.headline: US officials visit Palestinian village after settler attacks on diplomats
sources.text: TAYBEH, WEST BANK/JERUSALEM – US diplomats visited a Christian Palestinian town in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Oct 18, following attacks by militant Israeli settlers on European diplomats and an American photojournalist in the previous two days.Riley Barnes, Assistant Secretary of State for democracy, human rights and labour; Brian Burch, US ambassador to the Holy See; and a number of other diplomats visited the Latin Convent church and were expected to meet members of the Christian community in Taybeh.Belgian, French and Polish diplomats, along with a French mayor and Palestinian civilians, had been attacked near Taybeh on Oct 17 by masked Israeli settlers.The previous day, Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was taken to hospital after being assaulted while covering a Palestinian olive harvest near another West Bank village.The diplomats' visit coincided with US President Donald Trump endorsing his ally, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, for Israel’s parliamentary election on Oct 27.Netanyahu circumspect on settler violenceTrump has this year expressed his opposition to settlement expansion, but his administration has put little pressure on Netanyahu’s right-wing, pro-settler government to change its policy.UN bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law, but Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied.While Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and the Israeli military (IDF) both blamed “Israeli rioters” for the attack on the diplomats, Netanyahu – whose coalition is projected to lose its governing majority – has been more circumspect.He has said the diplomats entered a “sensitive area with a history of confrontations without prior coordination with the IDF”, and that the facts of the attack on Levine are “unclear”.France urged Israeli authorities to arrest the Oct 17 attackers and to end criminal violence in the West Bank, but by Oct 18, there was no announcement from Israeli authorities of any arrests in either of the two latest incidents.The West Bank is home to some 500,000 settlers and at least three million Palestinians.Settler attacks on the Palestinians are surging, with at least 170 since Sept 27, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli human rights group. Journalists, activists and foreign observers have also been targeted.Yet prosecutions of Israeli settlers are rare.On Oct 18, Reuters saw a group of at least 10 settlers, masked and dressed in black, hurling rocks at Palestinians and activists harvesting olives near the Palestinian West Bank town of Salfit, prompting the farmers to flee.Israeli border police were in the area and shot tear gas towards the hills. REUTERS
